facts.text: Collision during an intentional loading or spotting approach is ranked ninth by harm among the collision situations compared.
facts.quote: | 9 | Collision during an intentional loading or spotting approach

facts.text: Intentional loading or spotting approaches include trucks spotting under a loader or shovel or beside a stockpile, with slow reverse or forward movement.
facts.quote: Truck spotting under a loader, shovel or beside a stockpile; slow reverse or forward

facts.text: An intentional loading or spotting approach can cause high harm if another vehicle or person intrudes; otherwise, the approach is primarily a nuisance-alarm opportunity.
facts.quote: High if another vehicle or person intrudes; otherwise the main nuisance-alarm opportunity

facts.text: Normal loading or spotting approaches occur many times per shift.
facts.quote: Normal task occurs many times per shift

facts.text: An accident rate for intentional loading or spotting approaches was not found.
facts.quote: accident rate **not found**

facts.text: A loader rolled over during stockpile loading in New Zealand in 2017.
facts.quote: a loader rollover during stockpile loading (New Zealand, 2017)

facts.text: The collision-mitigation algorithm must distinguish an intended loading or spotting approach from an intrusion into the same space.
facts.quote: The algorithm must separate an intended approach from an intrusion into the same space

facts.text: Contact with a fixed structure, wall, stockpile or infrastructure is ranked tenth by harm among the collision situations compared.
facts.quote: | 10 | Contact with a fixed structure, wall, stockpile or infrastructure

facts.text: Contact with fixed structures, walls, stockpiles or infrastructure involves low-speed manoeuvring, reversing and side clearance across all machine types.
facts.quote: Low-speed manoeuvring, reversing, side clearance; all machine types

facts.text: Contact with fixed structures, walls, stockpiles or infrastructure usually causes low personnel harm but can cause high property loss.
facts.quote: Usually low personnel harm; potentially high property loss

facts.text: A light vehicle was reported as severely damaged against a decline wall.
facts.quote: light vehicle "severely damaged" against a decline wall

facts.text: Reliable frequency and cost data for contact with fixed structures, walls, stockpiles or infrastructure were not found.
facts.quote: Reliable frequency and cost data **not found**

facts.text: Queensland lists contact with fixed structures, walls, stockpiles or infrastructure as a high-potential collision class.
facts.quote: listed as a high-potential class by Queensland

facts.text: During manoeuvring near fixed structures, walls, stockpiles or infrastructure, sensors encounter real objects that are often intended to be close to the machine.
facts.quote: Sensors see real objects that are often supposed to be close

facts.text: Swing or rotation contact is ranked eleventh by harm among the collision situations compared.
facts.quote: | 11 | Swing or rotation contact

facts.text: Swing or rotation contact involves excavators, shovels and rotating upper structures and can be fatal.
facts.quote: Excavators, shovels, rotating upper structures | Potentially fatal

facts.text: The frequency of swing or rotation contact was not found, and agency statistics do not distinguish swing events.
facts.quote: Frequency **not found**; agency statistics do not separate swing

facts.text: Swing or rotation contact has different geometry from other collision situations.
facts.quote: Different geometry

facts.text: ISO 21815-4, described as under publication, treats rotation separately and relies mainly on motion inhibition before rotation.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-4 treats rotation separately and relies mainly on motion inhibition before rotation | Technical standard (under publication)

facts.text: The most frequently reported events in NSW, Queensland and New Zealand are machine-to-machine and machine-to-light-vehicle near misses and damage collisions.
facts.quote: The most frequently reported events are machine-to-machine and machine-to-light-vehicle near misses and damage collisions (NSW, Queensland, New Zealand).

facts.text: In US surface mining, fatal event types rank by frequency as berm and dump-edge events first, forward-travel crushes of light vehicles second, and reversing over pedestrians third.
facts.quote: The most frequent fatal event types in US surface mining are berm and dump-edge events, then forward-travel crushes of light vehicles, then reversing over pedestrians.

facts.text: In the one New Zealand quarter with a published vehicle-event breakdown, plant-to-plant collisions accounted for 11% of vehicle events, behind overturning at 46% and unintended movement or brake failure at 27%.
facts.quote: In the one New Zealand quarter with a published breakdown, plant-to-plant collisions were 11% of vehicle events, behind overturning (46%) and unintended movement or brake failure (27%) [30].
